title: Dave Jones at 225, Chinatown, Celestin and Ridgley, and the stolen banjo
summary: He names the 225 band lineup, building a name at Chinatown, moving among Celestin and Ridgley, and how friends stole his banjo to force him onto guitar.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I started organizing my combos. I was working down in the old district down there at uh, 225 with David Jones. Well it was Elric Kuyfer on trumpet. And uh, Boyd Millett playing piano at that time. Henry Russell.

Who was playing drums. And uh, David Jones, who was the managing band playing piano. And uh, April Associates was playing alto. And I left there. And I come up to uh, uh, uh, I got a job at Laiola and 8th, what they call Chinatown. Well I built up a name for myself, you know, through that. And then uh, ending out I was playing with Celestane's band, Papa Celestane. But I'd go back to my own outfit. Then I played with uh, uh, Ridgely, William Ridgely, used to live on Edinburgh Street.

I played with his band a while. And then uh, moved Johnny Censier. He come back from uh, out of Chicago. And then he started. After I left out of there, I started back my own group. And I played my own group up until, well up at the present, I get a little gist when I usually work a lot by myself. You know, entertain guitar and band. I played with them. And sing. When did you switch the guitar? You were playing band, most of the other bands. Well uh, I uh, right after, during the war, uh, John Patterson, Miss Kimball, and I and uh, it was Joe Harris, and uh, this guy Twat played bass across the river, and uh, and was another drum player, he died, I think Alvin, Alvin, uh, Clemens, he was playing drums at that time. And uh, well uh, Joe Robeshoe and Alan Gaudet played a trick on me, stole my banjo to make me get on guitar. So I swam from guitar, no banjo. They were in the band huh, Robeshoe and Alan Gaudet? No they were friends of mine, but Joe Robeshoe was working down, down at uh, with this guy at Pete Harmon's Club, his brother down there, you know his brother had that. Galata? Galata, he was working down there. Gaspar. He was working down there with two pianos, with uh, with Adam Kato and Joe Robeshoe. Oh yeah. Yeah, and they went to C-Rolls after that, you understand? There was two pianos, you know, they were doubling on pianos.
See, they went to C-Rolls? Yeah. C-Roll, Caliphas?
